title: Choose the visual world for Kevin Ding's Lab Notebook
question: The roll assigned Topographic Route & Hold Wall (Candidate #7). Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Topographic Route & Hold Wall
options.lineage: Indoor bouldering route-setting boards & Yosemite/Crag topographic guidebooks
options.thesis: Engineering systems graded as climbing problems on a chalk-dusted slate wall connected by vector route lines.
options.viewport: Full-viewport route board: Kevin's credentials pinned to the top ledger while SVG route lines link into three live interactive instrument plates (StressAlpha DCF tree, PokéBastion 28x18 pathfinder, Sapling graph).
options.risk: Climbing grades (V4-V8) must immediately map to real systems complexity rather than feeling like an inside joke.

raised.raise: Adopted deterministic fixed-slot tabular cell masks for all live DCF valuation and A* telemetry counters so numbers swap without layout jitter.
Adopted multi-field force routing so live vector paths dynamically bend around project holds and interactive obstacles.
Adopted registered before/after stress-state columns so every slider move shows baseline vs. stressed valuation delta side-by-side.
Adopted a hidden personal landmark mark tucked into each section and one deliberate spot color per problem plate.

options.label: Dieter Rams / Braun Technical Manual
options.lineage: 1960s Braun technical manuals & Ulm School instrument specifications
options.thesis: Every software project presented as a precision hardware specimen sheet with live rotary/slider controls.
options.viewport: Asymmetric specimen sheet with exposed millimeter rules, hosting live StressAlpha DCF dials and the 28x18 PokéBastion grid inside a recessed instrument bay.
options.risk: Familiar industrial-minimalist territory that many senior engineering portfolios gravitate toward.

options.label: Rietveld Sliding Planes
options.lineage: Rietveld Schröder house (1924) — sliding architectural partitions
options.thesis: One continuous architectural room where sliding primary-color joints reconfigure the viewport between live simulations and the off-hours life log.
options.viewport: A partitioned architectural plane where dragging or clicking the red, blue, and yellow structural edges slides open StressAlpha, PokéBastion, and the Life Log in place.
options.case: Fuses brilliantly with multi-pane interactive simulations where routes are plane positions rather than separate pages.
options.risk: Can feel rigidly architectural if the interactive game and financial widgets don't breathe inside the frames.

options.label: HyperCard Shoebox Stack
options.thesis: A tactile black-and-white dithered card stack where every project card is both a readable memo and an editable, playable tool.
options.viewport: A fixed-proportion HyperCard stack on a stippled desktop where visitors flip between playable StressAlpha, PokéBastion, and Sapling cards with live tool palettes.
options.case: Honors the 'tool for reading is the tool for making' ethos of a lab notebook.
options.risk: Strict 1-bit monochrome strips out the semantic color cues useful for financial heatmaps and game sprites.

options.label: Seven-Segment Totem
options.lineage: Eight-cell LED segment masks & scoreboard totems
options.thesis: A rigid near-black mask of lit red, amber, and green segment cells where digits and states ignite in place.
options.viewport: A dark scoreboard totem quoting $KVIN metrics and project states in giant segment digits.
options.case: Fuses poorly with long-form architectural writing and graph exploration.
options.kept: Fixed-slot tabular cell discipline with ghost unlit states for live telemetry readouts.
options.risk: Eight-cell masks cannot carry rich architectural memos or spatial node graphs cleanly.

options.label: Gravity-Rain Garden
options.thesis: A surreal vector-field garden where data drops orbit and fall toward project nodes according to cloud color.
options.viewport: A physics-driven garden canvas where blue and red rain streams bend around Kevin's project habitats.
options.case: Surreal curved baselines sacrifice scanability for hiring managers evaluating systems rigor.
options.kept: Interactive multi-field vector routing where particles dynamically bend around placed obstacles.
options.risk: Tilted baselines undermine technical credibility for a senior systems engineer.

options.label: Blacksmith Scale & Power Hammer
options.thesis: Forge-dark steel graded from black to white heat where each interaction strikes and lengthens the billet.
options.viewport: Full-width industrial rows ruled like a smith's chalk marks showing force numerals and deformed geometry.
options.case: Heavy blacksmith metallurgy feels disconnected from financial modeling, Pokémon TD, and knowledge graphs.
options.kept: Registered before-and-after comparison geometry with chalk-ruled tabular force deltas.
options.risk: Overly aggressive industrial metaphor for software and ML systems.

options.label: Mid-Century Editorial Issue
options.lineage: Art Paul's mid-century magazine grid & hidden cover mark
options.thesis: A strict two-column serif magazine issue with one editorial spot color per project and a hidden mark in every view.
options.viewport: A serif masthead over a two-column editorial spread with drop initials and an embedded interactive illustration plate.
options.case: Static magazine columns prioritize long interviews over simultaneous multi-instrument manipulation.
options.kept: Per-section editorial spot color custom property and a hidden signature mark tucked into each view.
options.risk: Reads like an essay archive rather than an interactive engineering lab.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: Clean dark-mode developer portfolio with bento cards and monospace badges, executed at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Centered developer intro above a three-card bento showcase with live interactive embeds.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from standard Vercel/Linear-inspired developer portfolios by design.
